# Recorded exploration instruction

Restate the exact target, hypotheses, parameter ranges, and what evidence would change the research direction. Before a long proof attempt, choose a cheap discriminating test. Consider at most three genuinely distinct approaches, identifying the first difficult implication in each. Use boundary cases, examples, counterexamples, or source applicability checks to select the next step.

Keep the original statement when changing a hypothesis or conclusion. Record the relationship between statements. Explain failed approaches through their mathematical obstruction. State every unproved dependency explicitly. Keep correctness, fidelity, and novelty separate. Numerical evidence is not a proof. Do not claim completion from a dependency graph alone.

Checkpoint exact current state, useful evidence, strongest objection, and next action after every response. Prefer decisive small results over repeated broad reductions. Your result will undergo independent reconstruction followed by critique. Neither step establishes mathematical acceptance automatically.
